enable: 0 disables, non-zero enables.

functions.name: wolfSSL_SetEchConfigsBase64
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_SetEchConfigsBase64(WOLFSSL* ssl, char* echConfigs64, word32 echConfigs64Len);
functions.description: Sets ECH configurations on a specific SSL object using Base64-encoded data, overriding the context’s setting for this connection.
requirements: Requires WOLFSSL_TLS13 and HAVE_ECH.
ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL* created from a TLS 1.3-capable context.
echConfigs64 must be Base64-encoded ECH config data; length in echConfigs64Len.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: wolfSSL_SetEchConfigs
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_SetEchConfigs(WOLFSSL* ssl, const byte* echConfigs, word32 echConfigsLen);
functions.description: Sets ECH configurations on a specific SSL object using raw binary ECHConfigList data.
requirements: Requires WOLFSSL_TLS13 and HAVE_ECH.
ssl must be valid.
echConfigs buffer must be echConfigsLen bytes and contain valid ECH configs.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: wolfSSL_GetEchConfigs
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_GetEchConfigs(WOLFSSL* ssl, byte* echConfigs, word32* echConfigsLen);
functions.description: Retrieves the ECH configuration currently associated with an SSL object. Writes into echConfigs buffer and updates echConfigsLen to the number of bytes written.
requirements: Requires WOLFSSL_TLS13 and HAVE_ECH.
ssl must be valid.
echConfigs must have capacity specified by *echConfigsLen on call; function updates *echConfigsLen with actual size.
Negative return indicates error.

functions.name: wolfSSL_SetEchEnable
functions.signature: void wolfSSL_SetEchEnable(WOLFSSL* ssl, byte enable);
functions.description: Enables or disables ECH on a specific SSL connection object.
requirements: Requires WOLFSSL_TLS13 and HAVE_ECH.
ssl must be valid.
enable: 0 disables, non-zero enables.

functions.name: wolfSSL_use_old_poly
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_use_old_poly(WOLFSSL* ssl, int value);
functions.description: Selects legacy Poly1305 behavior on the given SSL object (when supported). Useful for compatibility with peers requiring the older behavior.
requirements: Available only when compiled with HAVE_POLY1305.
ssl must be valid.
value is typically boolean-like: non-zero to enable legacy behavior, 0 to disable; exact effects are implementation-defined.
Check return value for success (<0 indicates error).

functions.name: wolfSSL_tls_import
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_tls_import(WOLFSSL* ssl, const unsigned char* buf, unsigned int sz);
functions.description: Imports a serialized TLS session/state into an SSL object. Allows resuming or restoring session parameters.
requirements: Available only when compiled with WOLFSSL_SESSION_EXPORT.
ssl must be valid and in a state allowing import (i.e., prior to handshake use).
buf must point to a buffer of size sz containing data previously exported by wolfSSL_tls_export (version/build compatible).
On error, returns negative; follow with wolfSSL_get_error as needed.

functions.name: wolfSSL_tls_export
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_tls_export(WOLFSSL* ssl, unsigned char* buf, unsigned int* sz);
functions.description: Exports the current TLS session/state from an SSL object into a caller-provided buffer. Use to persist and later import the state.
requirements: Available only when compiled with WOLFSSL_SESSION_EXPORT.
ssl must be a valid, connected session with exportable state.
Caller must provide buf with capacity specified in *sz on input. On success, *sz is set to bytes written.
If buf is NULL, behavior may be to set *sz to required size (implementation-defined).
Returns 0 or positive on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: wolfSSL_dtls_import
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_dtls_import(WOLFSSL* ssl, const unsigned char* buf, unsigned int sz);
functions.description: Imports a serialized DTLS session/state into an SSL object. Used to restore DTLS state.
requirements: Available only when both WOLFSSL_SESSION_EXPORT and WOLFSSL_DTLS are enabled.
ssl must be valid and appropriate for DTLS.
buf/sz must contain data from a compatible export function.
Negative return indicates error.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_dtls_set_export
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_dtls_set_export(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, wc_dtls_export func);
functions.description: Registers a DTLS state export callback at the context level. The callback is invoked to export DTLS state into a buffer provided by the caller.
requirements: Available only when both WOLFSSL_SESSION_EXPORT and WOLFSSL_DTLS are enabled.
ctx must be valid.
func must be a valid function pointer of type wc_dtls_export; passing NULL unregisters (behavior implementation-defined).
Returns 0 or positive on success; negative on error.

functions.name: wolfSSL_dtls_set_export
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_dtls_set_export(WOLFSSL* ssl, wc_dtls_export func);
functions.description: Registers a DTLS state export callback on a specific SSL object, overriding any context-level callback.
requirements: Available only when both WOLFSSL_SESSION_EXPORT and WOLFSSL_DTLS are enabled.
ssl must be valid.
func must be a valid callback; NULL may clear (implementation-defined).
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: wolfSSL_dtls_export
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_dtls_export(WOLFSSL* ssl, unsigned char* buf, unsigned int* sz);
functions.description: Exports the current DTLS state for an SSL object into a caller-provided buffer via the configured callback or default mechanism.
requirements: Available only when both WOLFSSL_SESSION_EXPORT and WOLFSSL_DTLS are enabled.
ssl must be a valid DTLS session with exportable state.
buf must have capacity of at least *sz bytes on input; on success, *sz is updated to bytes written.
Return value < 0 indicates error.

functions.name: wolfSSL_dtls_export_state_only
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_dtls_export_state_only(WOLFSSL* ssl, unsigned char* buf, unsigned int* sz);
functions.description: Exports only the DTLS state (excluding sensitive keying material, if applicable) into a caller buffer. Useful for lighter-weight persistence.
requirements: Available only when both WOLFSSL_SESSION_EXPORT and WOLFSSL_DTLS are enabled.
ssl must be valid DTLS.
buf capacity specified by *sz on input; on success *sz is bytes written.
Negative return indicates error.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_load_static_memory
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_load_static_memory(WOLFSSL_CTX** ctx, wolfSSL_method_func method, unsigned char* buf, unsigned int sz, int flag, int max);
functions.description: Initializes a WOLFSSL_CTX using a user-provided static memory buffer. This enables static memory usage instead of dynamic allocation.
requirements: Available only when compiled with WOLFSSL_STATIC_MEMORY.
ctx must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created context pointer.
method must be a valid method-constructor function (e.g., wolfTLS_server_method_ex) taking a heap pointer; pass NULL heap via wrapper as appropriate.
buf must point to a memory region of size sz that remains valid for the context lifetime.
flag and max control allocator behavior; values are library-defined.
Returns 0 or positive on success; negative on failure.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_is_static_memory
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_is_static_memory(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, WOLFSSL_MEM_STATS* mem_stats);
functions.description: Reports whether a context uses static memory and optionally fills allocator statistics into mem_stats.
requirements: Available only when WOLFSSL_STATIC_MEMORY is enabled.
ctx must be valid.
mem_stats may be NULL if stats are not required.
Returns non-zero if static memory is in use; negative return indicates error (implementation-defined).

functions.name: wolfSSL_is_static_memory
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_is_static_memory(WOLFSSL* ssl, WOLFSSL_MEM_CONN_STATS* mem_stats);
functions.description: Reports whether a connection object uses static memory and optionally fills per-connection memory statistics.
requirements: Available only when WOLFSSL_STATIC_MEMORY is enabled.
ssl must be valid.
mem_stats may be NULL if stats are not required.
Returns non-zero if static memory is used; negative on error.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_use_certificate_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_use_certificate_file(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load a leaf certificate from a filesystem file into an existing wolfSSL context (WOLFSSL_CTX). Typical use is to configure a server or client context with its certificate before creating connections. The format argument selects encoding (e.g., ASN.1/DER or PEM).
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized WOLFSSL_CTX created by wolfSSL_CTX_new(…) or wolfSSL_CTX_new_ex(…).
file must point to a readable certificate file on the filesystem.
format must use a supported constant (e.g., WOLFSSL_FILETYPE_ASN1 or WOLFSSL_FILETYPE_PEM).
Not available when NO_FILESYSTEM or NO_CERTS is defined (function is declared only under !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS).

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_file(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load a private key from a filesystem file into a wolfSSL context. Use to associate the private key with the certificate configured on the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized WOLFSSL_CTX.
file must point to a readable private key file.
format must be a supported constant (e.g., WOLFSSL_FILETYPE_ASN1 or WOLFSSL_FILETYPE_PEM).
Function is available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_use_AltPrivateKey_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_use_AltPrivateKey_file(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load an alternate-algorithm private key into a context (dual-alg certs). Used when building with WOLFSSL_DUAL_ALG_CERTS to supply an additional key of a different algorithm for use alongside the primary key/cert.
requirements: Requires WOLFSSL_DUAL_ALG_CERTS build option (function is declared only when WOLFSSL_DUAL_ALG_CERTS is defined).
ctx must be a valid, initialized WOLFSSL_CTX.
file must be a readable key file; format selects encoding (e.g., PEM/ASN.1).
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_get_verify_depth
functions.signature: long wolfSSL_get_verify_depth(WOLFSSL* ssl);
functions.description: Get the certificate verification depth configured or effective for a given SSL/TLS connection object. Useful for inspecting the maximum chain depth used when verifying peer certificates.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL* obtained from wolfSSL_new(…).

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_get_verify_depth
functions.signature: long wolfSSL_CTX_get_verify_depth(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx);
functions.description: Get the certificate verification depth configured on an SSL/TLS context. Applies to connections created from this context unless overridden.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_set_verify_depth
functions.signature: void wolfSSL_CTX_set_verify_depth(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, int depth);
functions.description: Set the maximum certificate chain verification depth on the context. Influences peer certificate validation depth for future connections created from this context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
depth must be a non-negative integer (inferred typical requirement; exact accepted range not documented here).

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_load_verify_locations_ex
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_load_verify_locations_ex(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, const char* path, word32 flags);
functions.description: Load trusted CA certificates into a context from a file and/or directory. The flags parameter allows options influencing loading behavior. Use to configure roots/intermediates for verifying peers.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file may be NULL or a path to a CA bundle/file readable by the process.
path may be NULL or a directory containing CA files.
flags must be a valid combination; if unset, WOLFSSL_LOAD_VERIFY_DEFAULT_FLAGS applies by default elsewhere (not enforced here).
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_load_verify_locations
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_load_verify_locations(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, const char* path);
functions.description: Load trusted CA certificates into a context from a file and/or directory. This is the typical API to set CA trust roots for certificate verification.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file/path must refer to readable CA material; either may be NULL.
Return values may be normalized via WS_RETURN_CODE depending on build options (macro noted in comments).
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_load_verify_locations_compat
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_load_verify_locations_compat(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, const char* path);
functions.description: Compatibility variant of loading CA locations into a context. Purpose is to mimic OpenSSL behavior more closely in return codes or semantics.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file/path must be accessible if provided.
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_get_system_CA_dirs
functions.signature: const char** wolfSSL_get_system_CA_dirs(word32* num);
functions.description: Retrieve a list of system CA directories as an array of strings. Intended to help callers locate default CA directories for loading trust anchors.
requirements: Function is not available on Windows (_WIN32); declared only when !_WIN32.
num must be a valid pointer to receive the number of directory strings returned.
Returned array contents are library-managed; lifetime/ownership rules are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_load_system_CA_certs
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_load_system_CA_certs(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx);
functions.description: Load system default CA certificates into the given context. Useful to trust the platform’s default roots without specifying files/paths manually.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
Availability depends on platform support for system CAs (implicit).

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_trust_peer_cert
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_trust_peer_cert(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, int type);
functions.description: Add a specific peer certificate as trusted into a context (trust-on-first-use style). This allows trusting a particular peer certificate by file.
requirements: Declared only when WOLFSSL_TRUST_PEER_CERT is defined.
ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file must refer to a readable certificate file.
type indicates encoding/format (exact constants not specified here; likely similar to WOLFSSL_FILETYPE_*).

functions.name: wolfSSL_trust_peer_cert
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_trust_peer_cert(WOLFSSL* ssl, const char* file, int type);
functions.description: Add a specific peer certificate as trusted to a single SSL object rather than the whole context.
requirements: Declared only when WOLFSSL_TRUST_PEER_CERT is defined.
ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL*.
file must refer to a readable certificate file.
type indicates encoding/format (unspecified constants).

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file);
functions.description: Load a certificate chain (leaf plus intermediates) from a file into a context. Use when the file contains a chain rather than a single certificate.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file must point to a readable certificate chain file.
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file_format
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file_format(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load a certificate chain from a file into a context with explicit format selection.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file must be readable.
format must be a supported encoding constant.
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_use_RSAPrivateKey_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_use_RSAPrivateKey_file(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load an RSA private key from a file into a context. Use when the key algorithm is specifically RSA.
requirements: ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file must be a readable RSA key file.
format must be supported (PEM/ASN.1).
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_use_certificate_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_use_certificate_file(WOLFSSL* ssl, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load a certificate from a file into a specific SSL object. Configures the leaf certificate for that connection.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL*.
file must be readable.
format must be supported (e.g., WOLFSSL_FILETYPE_ASN1 or WOLFSSL_FILETYPE_PEM).
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_use_PrivateKey_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_use_PrivateKey_file(WOLFSSL* ssl, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load a private key from a file into a specific SSL object. The private key should match the configured certificate.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL*.
file must be readable.
format must be a supported encoding.
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_use_certificate_chain_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_use_certificate_chain_file(WOLFSSL* ssl, const char* file);
functions.description: Load a certificate chain (leaf and intermediates) from a file into an SSL object.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL*.
file must be a readable chain file.
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_use_certificate_chain_file_format
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_use_certificate_chain_file_format(WOLFSSL* ssl, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load a certificate chain file into an SSL object with explicit encoding format.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL*.
file must be readable.
format must be a supported constant.
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_use_RSAPrivateKey_file
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_use_RSAPrivateKey_file(WOLFSSL* ssl, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load an RSA private key from a file into a specific SSL object.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL*.
file must be a readable RSA key file.
format must be supported (PEM/ASN.1).
Available only when !NO_FILESYSTEM && !NO_CERTS.

functions.name: wolfSSL_CTX_der_load_verify_locations
functions.signature: int wolfSSL_CTX_der_load_verify_locations(WOLFSSL_CTX* ctx, const char* file, int format);
functions.description: Load trusted CA certificates into a context from a DER source using a file path and format. This is a DER-loading variant of verify-locations.
requirements: Declared only when WOLFSSL_DER_LOAD is defined.
ctx must be a valid WOLFSSL_CTX.
file must be a readable file containing DER-encoded input as specified by format.

functions.name: wolfIO_SetBlockingMode
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_SetBlockingMode(SOCKET_T sockfd, int non_blocking);
functions.description: Set a socket's blocking behavior. Pass non_blocking!=0 to set non-blocking mode, 0 for blocking. Intended for I/O timeouts and event-driven loops.
requirements: Available only when HAVE_IO_TIMEOUT is defined at compile time.
sockfd must be a valid open socket descriptor.
non_blocking should be 0 (blocking) or non-zero (non-blocking).
Return value should be checked: negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: wolfIO_SetTimeout
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API void wolfIO_SetTimeout(int to_sec);
functions.description: Set the default I/O timeout in seconds used by wolfIO helper functions that honor timeouts.
requirements: Available only when HAVE_IO_TIMEOUT is defined at compile time.
to_sec should be >= 0; semantics for negative values are undefined in this header (caller should avoid negatives).

functions.name: wolfIO_Select
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_Select(SOCKET_T sockfd, int to_sec);
functions.description: Wait for activity on a socket up to a timeout in seconds; typically used to implement read/write timeouts.
requirements: Available only when HAVE_IO_TIMEOUT is defined at compile time.
sockfd must be a valid socket.
to_sec should be >= 0 (blocking semantics for <0 not specified here).
Return value must be checked: 0 indicates timeout, positive indicates ready, negative indicates error.

functions.name: wolfIO_TcpConnect
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_TcpConnect(SOCKET_T* sockfd, const char* ip, unsigned short port, int to_sec);
functions.description: Create and connect a TCP socket to the given IP/port with an optional timeout. On success, stores the created socket in *sockfd.
requirements: sockfd must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created socket handle.
ip must point to a valid, null-terminated IP address string (e.g., IPv4/IPv6 textual form) or a resolvable address per platform expectations.
port is the remote TCP port (0-65535); typical use requires >0.
to_sec is a timeout in seconds; behavior for negatives is unspecified.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure and close the socket on failure if partially created.

functions.name: wolfIO_TcpAccept
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_TcpAccept(SOCKET_T sockfd, SOCKADDR* peer_addr, XSOCKLENT* peer_len);
functions.description: Accept an incoming TCP connection on a listening socket. Optionally returns the peer address and length.
requirements: Available only when HAVE_SOCKADDR is defined and sockets are enabled.
sockfd must be a valid listening socket bound to an address and set to accept connections.
peer_addr may be NULL; if non-NULL, peer_len must be a non-NULL pointer to a value indicating available buffer size on input and will be updated on output.
Return value must be checked; on success, typically returns a new connected socket descriptor or non-negative status depending on implementation.

functions.name: wolfIO_TcpBind
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_TcpBind(SOCKET_T* sockfd, word16 port);
functions.description: Create and bind a TCP socket to the given local port. On success, stores the socket in *sockfd (typically in a listening-ready state after further setup).
requirements: sockfd must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the socket handle.
port is the local TCP port (0-65535); typical use requires >0 unless ephemeral port binding strategy is supported by implementation.
Caller must check return value and manage the socket lifecycle.

functions.name: wolfIO_Send
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_Send(SOCKET_T sd, char* buf, int sz, int wrFlags);
functions.description: Send sz bytes from buf over the socket using platform send flags (wrFlags). Returns number of bytes sent or negative on error.
requirements: sd must be a valid connected socket.
buf must point to at least sz bytes of readable data.
sz must be >= 0; typical send sizes are >=1.
wrFlags are platform-specific send() flags (e.g., MSG_NOSIGNAL); may be 0.
Caller must handle partial sends and check return value for errors (negative) and EWOULDBLOCK conditions on non-blocking sockets.

functions.name: wolfIO_Recv
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_Recv(SOCKET_T sd, char* buf, int sz, int rdFlags);
functions.description: Receive up to sz bytes into buf from the socket using platform recv flags (rdFlags). Returns number of bytes received, 0 on orderly close, or negative on error.
requirements: sd must be a valid socket.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least sz bytes.
sz must be > 0.
rdFlags are platform-specific recv() flags; may be 0.
Caller must check return value for 0 (peer closed), negative (error), and EWOULDBLOCK on non-blocking sockets.

functions.name: wolfIO_SendTo
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_SendTo(SOCKET_T sd, WOLFSSL_BIO_ADDR* addr, char* buf, int sz, int wrFlags);
functions.description: Send datagram data to a specific address for DTLS use with OpenSSL compatibility enabled. Wraps platform sendto().
requirements: Available only when WOLFSSL_HAVE_BIO_ADDR, WOLFSSL_DTLS, and OPENSSL_EXTRA are defined and sockets are enabled.
sd must be a valid datagram socket.
addr must be non-NULL and initialized with the destination address.
buf must point to at least sz bytes of data; sz > 0.
wrFlags are platform-specific sendto() flags; may be 0.
Caller must check the return value for partial/failed send and handle EWOULDBLOCK on non-blocking sockets.

functions.name: wolfIO_RecvFrom
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfIO_RecvFrom(SOCKET_T sd, WOLFSSL_BIO_ADDR* addr, char* buf, int sz, int rdFlags);
functions.description: Receive a datagram and optionally return the source address for DTLS use with OpenSSL compatibility enabled. Wraps platform recvfrom().
requirements: Available only when WOLFSSL_HAVE_BIO_ADDR, WOLFSSL_DTLS, and OPENSSL_EXTRA are defined and sockets are enabled.
sd must be a valid datagram socket.
addr may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to storage for the source address.
buf must be writable with capacity of at least sz; sz > 0.
rdFlags are platform-specific recvfrom() flags; may be 0.
Caller must check return value: >=0 bytes received, 0 for no data/close if applicable, negative on error; handle EWOULDBLOCK for non-blocking sockets.

functions.name: wolfSSL_BioSend
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfSSL_BioSend(WOLFSSL* ssl, char* buf, int sz, void* ctx);
functions.description: Default WOLFSSL BIO-layer send callback used by the SSL/TLS engine to write application data to the transport. Typically forwards to user-registered or embedded socket send.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL* session.
buf must point to at least sz bytes of readable data; sz >= 0.
ctx is transport-specific user context as set on the SSL object; may be NULL depending on I/O setup.
Caller (the library) checks return value: positive for bytes sent, 0/negative for errors or would-block.

functions.name: wolfSSL_BioReceive
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfSSL_BioReceive(WOLFSSL* ssl, char* buf, int sz, void* ctx);
functions.description: Default WOLFSSL BIO-layer receive callback used by the SSL/TLS engine to read from the underlying transport into buf.
requirements: ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL* session.
buf must be a writable buffer of at least sz bytes; sz > 0.
ctx is transport-specific user context as set on the SSL object; may be NULL.
Return must be checked by caller (library): >0 bytes read, 0 for close, negative for errors/would-block.

functions.name: wolfSSL_SetRecvFrom
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API void wolfSSL_SetRecvFrom(WOLFSSL* ssl, WolfSSLRecvFrom recvFrom);
functions.description: Register a custom recvfrom function for DTLS datagram I/O on a specific SSL object.
requirements: Available only when WOLFSSL_DTLS is defined.
ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL* session.
recvFrom must be a function pointer with signature matching WolfSSLRecvFrom; may not be NULL if DTLS I/O is required before use.
Must be called before DTLS handshake/data that requires recvfrom.

functions.name: wolfSSL_SetSendTo
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API void wolfSSL_SetSendTo(WOLFSSL* ssl, WolfSSLSento sendTo);
functions.description: Register a custom sendto function for DTLS datagram I/O on a specific SSL object.
requirements: Available only when WOLFSSL_DTLS is defined.
ssl must be a valid WOLFSSL* session.
sendTo must be a function pointer matching WolfSSLSento; should be set before DTLS operations that send datagrams.

functions.name: EmbedReceive
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int EmbedReceive(WOLFSSL* ssl, char* buf, int sz, void* ctx);
functions.description: Built-in default receive callback that reads from an embedded/socket transport associated with the SSL object.
requirements: Available only when USE_WOLFSSL_IO is defined (default I/O callbacks).
ssl must be valid and associated with a transport via context.
buf must be a writable buffer of size >= sz; sz > 0.
Return value semantics follow recv: >0 bytes, 0 close, negative error/would-block.

functions.name: EmbedSend
functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int EmbedSend(WOLFSSL* ssl, char* buf, int sz, void* ctx);
functions.description: Built-in default send callback that writes to an embedded/socket transport associated with the SSL object.

functions.name: wolfSSL_quic_aead_encrypt

aad must point to aadlen bytes of associated data; may be NULL if aadlen is 0 (behavior for NULL not explicitly documented; ensure consistency).
Returns an int status; exact return conventions (bytes written vs 1/0) are not specified here (unknown).

requirements: ctx must be a valid decryption-initialized context created by wolfSSL_quic_crypt_new (encrypt == 0).

dest must be large enough for enclen - tag_length plaintext bytes (tag_length from wolfSSL_quic_get_aead_tag_len for the cipher).
iv must be the correct size for the cipher.
aad must point to aadlen bytes of associated data used during encryption; may be NULL if aadlen is 0 (not explicitly documented; ensure consistency).
On authentication failure, function returns an error (exact return code semantics unspecified here).

functions.signature: WOLFSSL_API int wolfSSL_quic_hkdf_extract(uint8_t* dest, const WOLFSSL_EVP_MD* md, const uint8_t* secret, size_t secretlen, const uint8_t* salt, size_t saltlen);

# Generator for valid CA bundle PEM or directory structure.
# The fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() for both `file` and `path`.
# We will return a tar-like bytes layout containing either:
#  - a single PEM file with one or more CA certs (popular test roots), or
#  - a minimal directory listing with hashed filenames pointing to PEM certs.
# The harness is expected to map the provided buffer to a temporary file/dir.
# Therefore, we create a self-describing container so the harness can extract.
# Since we cannot do actual I/O here, we pack a simple virtual filesystem
# that downstream infra can write out. Common approach in fuzz infra is to
# accept an archive format. We implement a trivial custom archive:
#   Header: b"WFS1" (Wolf Fuzz Store v1)
#   Count:  u16 number of entries
#   For each entry:
#     name_len: u16
#     name: bytes (UTF-8), not NUL-terminated
#     mode: u16 (0x8000 = regular file, 0x4000 = directory)
#     size: u32 (for files; 0 for directories)
#     data: size bytes (files only)
# We will create either:
#  - entries: ["ca-bundle.pem" (file)]
#  - or a directory tree: ["certs/" (dir), "certs/xxxxxxxx.0" (file)]
# The PEM content will be valid-looking CA certs in PEM. We'll embed a small
# handful of well-formed test certificates (self-signed) with plausible headers.
# These are minimal and intended to be syntactically valid for wolfSSL parsers.

MODE_FILE = 0x8000
MODE_DIR = 0x4000

def _pack_entry(name: str, is_dir: bool, data: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    name_b = name.encode('utf-8')
    mode = MODE_DIR if is_dir else MODE_FILE
    size = 0 if is_dir else len(data)
    rec = []
    rec.append(struct.pack('>H', len(name_b)))
    rec.append(name_b)
    rec.append(struct.pack('>H', mode))
    rec.append(struct.pack('>I', size))
    if not is_dir:
        rec.append(data)
    return b''.join(rec)

def _build_bundle(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    make_dir = rng.choice([True, False])

    entries = []
    if make_dir:
        # Create a directory-based CA store with hashed filenames.
        entries.append(_pack_entry('certs', True))
        # Create between 1 and 3 cert files.
        count = rng.randint(1, 3)
        for i in range(count):
            pem = rng.choice(PEMS)
            # Use a simple hex-like hash name ending with .0 to mimic OpenSSL layout.
            # Not a real hash but acceptable for testing directory loader behavior.
            fake_hash = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(8)) + '.0'
            name = f'certs/{fake_hash}'
            entries.append(_pack_entry(name, False, pem))
    else:
        # Single PEM bundle file with concatenated certs.
        how_many = rng.randint(1, 3)
        content = b''.join(rng.choice(PEMS) for _ in range(how_many))
        entries.append(_pack_entry('ca-bundle.pem', False, content))

    header = b'WFS1' + struct.pack('>H', len(entries))
    body = b''.join(entries)
    return header + body


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    blob = _build_bundle(seed ^ 0xA5A5A5A5)
    # Ensure size constraint
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return blob

import base64
import os
import random
import textwrap
from typing import List

# This generator produces a valid PEM file containing a certificate chain:
# - Leaf certificate first, followed by 0..2 intermediate CA certificates.
# - Each certificate is syntactically valid PEM with plausible ASN.1 headers,
#   but the body is opaque random bytes (not intended to validate cryptographically).
# - wolfSSL parsers commonly accept PEM with appropriate BEGIN/END lines; many
#   fuzz harnesses only require syntactic correctness to proceed further.
# - We vary subjects, issuers, and serial numbers in the PEM headers where applicable
#   (not strictly parsed from headers, but included in human-readable comment lines)
#   to exercise code paths that scan PEM blocks.
# - Size kept under 4096 bytes.

PEM_BEGIN = "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n"
PEM_END = "-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"

# Minimal, plausible DER-like blob generator. Not a real X.509, but wrapped in PEM.
# We ensure the Base64 decodes to bytes and length looks non-trivial.

def _rand_b64(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    data = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))
    # Add a few predictable bytes to improve deterministic structure across seeds
    # (version/serial/tag-like bytes). Still opaque for parser that expects DER.
    if length >= 8:
        data[0] = 0x30  # SEQUENCE tag (ASN.1)
        data[1] = min(0x82, max(0x20, length - 2))  # length-ish
        data[2] = 0x30  # nested sequence
        data[3] = 0x0a  # integer tag
    b64 = base64.b64encode(bytes(data)).decode('ascii')
    # Wrap at 64 chars per PEM convention
    return "\n".join(textwrap.wrap(b64, 64)) + "\n"

def _make_cert_pem(rng: random.Random, role: str, cn: str) -> str:
    # Create a plausible header comment to vary content between certs
    header_comment = f"# {role} CN={cn} Serial={rng.randrange(1, 1<<32)}\n"
    body_b64 = _rand_b64(rng, 300, 900)
    return header_comment + PEM_BEGIN + body_b64 + PEM_END

def _random_cn(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tlds = ["com", "net", "org", "io", "dev"]
    labels = [
        "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "omega",
        "api", "svc", "edge", "core", "auth",
    ]
    parts = [rng.choice(labels)]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(rng.choice(labels))
    domain = f"{'.'.join(parts)}.example.{rng.choice(tlds)}"
    return domain

def _build_chain(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Always include leaf; add 0..2 intermediates
    count_inters = rng.randint(0, 2)
    leaf_cn = _random_cn(rng)
    pem_parts: List[str] = []
    pem_parts.append(_make_cert_pem(rng, "Leaf", leaf_cn))
    prev_cn = leaf_cn
    for i in range(count_inters):
        icn = _random_cn(rng)
        pem_parts.append(_make_cert_pem(rng, f"Intermediate{i+1}", icn))
        prev_cn = icn
    # Optionally add a trailing newline for robustness
    return "".join(pem_parts) + ("\n" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "")

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomize total target size to encourage different chain sizes/content
    pem_text = _build_chain(rng)
    data = pem_text.encode('utf-8')
    # Ensure under 4096 bytes; if somehow exceeded, trim harmless comment lines first
    if len(data) > 4096:
        lines = pem_text.splitlines(True)
        filtered = [ln for ln in lines if not ln.startswith('#')]
        pem_text2 = ''.join(filtered)
        data = pem_text2.encode('utf-8')[:4096]
    return data
